neighbours.label: the verb ' pressured' (someone pressured by others into doing something)
fire: Many young athletes feel pressured by coaches to play through injuries.
She said she was pressured into signing the contract that night.
The witnesses claimed they had been pressured by detectives to change their stories.
Teenagers are often pressured by classmates to try vaping.
Several judges felt pressured by the government to rule in its favour.
He never pressured his children to follow him into medicine.
Staff were pressured to hit unrealistic sales targets every month.
The farmers were pressured into selling their land below market value.
quiet: Many young athletes are supported by coaches to recover from injuries.
She said she was thrilled about signing the contract that night.
The witnesses claimed they had been interviewed by detectives at the station.
Teenagers are often taught by classmates how to use new apps.
Several judges were appointed by the government last spring.
He never expected his children to follow him into medicine.
Staff were rewarded for hitting their sales targets every month.
The farmers were happy with selling their land at market value.

notes: Top example is ' pressured'; told/ordered/encourage also appear but probed weaker (ordered 0.08, urged 0.04, forced 0.16 vs pressured 0.41). Tested at the word level.
